q_44877.question_text: Where will be the great white shark Percy on September 1, 2026?
q_44877.reasoning:
I'll work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

From today (July 28, 2026) to September 1, 2026 = approximately 35 days.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

**Current position (as of July 5-6, 2026):** Percy is off the east coast of Florida near Cocoa Beach.

**Migration pattern analysis:**
- Percy was tagged July 28, 2025 in Mahone Bay, Nova Scotia
- By April-May 2026, he had migrated south to the Florida Panhandle/Pensacola area
- By July 5-6, 2026, he was off central Florida (Cocoa Beach area), having moved north along the coast
- Research indicates great whites typically migrate south in colder months and north as waters warm
- May 2026 reporting suggested Percy had reached the end of his southern migration and would return to Nova Scotia

**Trajectory for September 1, 2026:**
With ~35 days remaining, Percy is currently on the Florida coast and appears to be in his northward migration phase. Given:
- The pattern of northward movement from May onward
- The typical migration behavior (returning to Nova Scotia as waters warm)
- He has 3,705 miles covered over 342 days, averaging ~10.8 miles/day
- In 35 days at this pace, he could cover ~380 miles

From Cocoa Beach (central Florida), moving north along the Atlantic coast:
- 380 miles north would place him somewhere in the Carolinas or potentially Virginia/Maryland range
- This aligns with the natural northward migration pattern documented

However, shark movements are inherently variable, and the exact trajectory depends on water temperature, prey availability, and ocean currents.

## (c) Key uncertainties

1. **Ping frequency and accuracy:** The resolution depends on "the most recent ping" as of September 1, 2026. We don't know how frequently Percy pings or if gaps in data might occur.

2. **Migration speed variability:** While the historical average is ~10.8 miles/day, this could vary significantly based on environmental conditions.

3. **Coastline proximity:** The question resolves based on "closest landmass due west" - this requires Percy to be relatively close to the coast. If he ventures offshore, the answer changes fundamentally.

4. **Exact migration destination:** While northward return to Nova Scotia is typical, the intermediate stopping points and pace are not perfectly predictable.

## Analysis of each option

- **Florida:** Percy is currently off Florida and moving north. By September 1, 35 days later, he will likely have traveled further north. ~15%

- **Georgia, South Carolina, or North Carolina:** Given the northward trajectory at ~11 mi/day pace and 35 days of travel, the Carolinas seem like the most probable intermediate destination. ~50%

- **Virginia or Maryland:** Further north than the Carolinas - possible if migration is faster or more direct, but less likely in this 35-day window. ~25%

- **Any other U.S. State:** Percy is moving along the Atlantic coast; unlikely to veer inland or westward significantly in 35 days. ~5%

- **Somewhere else:** Very unlikely given the documented pattern and timeframe. ~5%

**Option probabilities:**
Florida: 15%
Georgia, South Carolina, or North Carolina: 50%
Virginia or Maryland: 25%
Any other U.S. State: 5%
Somewhere else: 5%
q_44877.research_text:
As of July 5, 2026, the great white shark Percy was located off the east coast of Florida near Cocoa Beach [Gulf Coast Journeys citing Info from OCEARCH](https://www.facebook.com/GulfCoastJourneys/posts/percy-is-on-the-move-again-the-9-foot-9-inch-432-pound-great-white-is-now-off-th/955230944207870/). Percy, a sub-adult male measuring 9 feet 9 inches and weighing 432 pounds, was originally tagged by OCEARCH in Mahone Bay, Nova Scotia, on July 28, 2025 [pnj.com](https://www.pnj.com/story/news/local/pensacola/beaches/2026/05/13/great-white-shark-ping-pensacola-beach/90059786007/, [ocearch.org](https://www.ocearch.org/tracker/detail/percy). Since being tagged, he has traveled approximately 3,705 miles in 342 days [Gulf Coast Journeys citing Info from OCEARCH](https://www.facebook.com/GulfCoastJourneys/posts/percy-is-on-the-move-again-the-9-foot-9-inch-432-pound-great-white-is-now-off-th/955230944207870/).

Percy spent time off the Florida Panhandle and near Pensacola Beach in April and early May 2026, with pings recorded on April 21, April 26, May 6, and May 11 [pnj.com](https://www.pnj.com/story/news/local/pensacola/beaches/2026/05/13/great-white-shark-ping-pensacola-beach/90059786007/, [nola.com](https://www.nola.com/news/gulf_coast/great-white-shark-florida-coast/article_2856ab6a-6cb4-4c42-a19d-00927783393b9.html). Great white sharks typically migrate south along the eastern U.S. coastline in colder months and return north (towards Nova Scotia) as waters warm, with many leaving the Gulf of Mexico by mid-May [pnj.com](https://www.pnj.com/story/news/local/pensacola/beaches/2026/05/13/great-white-shark-ping-pensacola-beach/90059786007/, [wkrg.com](https://www.wkrg.com/northwest-florida/escambia-county/great-white-shark-tracked-near-coast-of-pensacola-beach/). It was suggested in May 2026 that Percy had likely reached the end of his migratory journey south and would begin returning to Nova Scotia [pnj.com](https://www.pnj.com/story/news/local/pensacola/beaches/2026/05/13/great-white-shark-ping-pensacola-beach/90059786007/).
